findings.title: Role/client/group removal cleanup listener now gated by the V1 feature flag only
findings.body: The ProviderEventListener body that disables permissions for a removed role/client/group (calling management(...).roles()/.clients()/.groups().setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) used to run unconditionally. This PR wraps the whole block in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`, i.e. it now only runs when the (older) V1 fine-grained-authz feature is enabled. The `management(...)` factory itself selects V1 vs V2 based on `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`, so if a deployment only enables the V2 feature (without V1), this cleanup listener will be skipped entirely and permission/resource cleanup for deleted roles/clients/groups will no longer happen for V2 permissions. This change is unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR (adding Clients resource type) and is not covered by any new test.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission cannot find per-client resources and leaks the catch-all resource name
findings.body: `getClientsWithPermission` looks up resources via `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`, which filters on the resource's `type` attribute. However, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (used to create the per-client resource when a scoped permission is created for a specific client) never calls `resource.setType(...)`; only the catch-all 'all-resource' entry created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` has its type set to `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`. As a result: (1) individual per-client resources will never be returned by `findByType`, so clients with a specific scoped permission are silently omitted from the result set, and (2) if the catch-all 'Clients' resource itself has the scope granted, its resource name ('Clients') is incorrectly added to the returned set as if it were a client id. Any caller treating the returned set as a list of client ids will get wrong/empty results.

findings.title: No migration path to add the new Clients resource/scopes for realms that already enabled admin permissions
findings.body: `init()` only creates the schema resources/scopes (including the newly added 'Clients' resource type and its scopes) when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient()` is null, i.e. only the very first time admin permissions are enabled for a realm. For any realm that already had admin fine-grained permissions (V2) enabled before this change was deployed, `init()` returns immediately and the 'Clients' resource/scope set is never created. Consequently, `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(...)` will call `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`, which returns null because the resource doesn't exist, and that null is then passed into `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`, risking an NPE (or at least silently returning no permissions) for any existing realm upgrading to this version. There is no migration/upgrade step shown to retrofit existing admin-permission-enabled realms with the new resource type.

findings.title: Missing tests for client-scope role mapping and for all-vs-single resource interaction
findings.body: There is no test exercising `canMapClientScopeRoles`/`MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` for clients (only MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE are covered in PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient), and no test for `getClientsWithPermission`, nor for the interaction between an 'all clients' grant and a resource that already exists for a specific client due to an unrelated scope permission (the analogous scenario is tested for Users in UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testImpersonatePermission but has no Clients counterpart). Given the fallback logic in `hasPermission` only triggers when no per-client resource exists at all, this combination is an important but untested code path.
